exampleAnswers.title: Identifying Elements Belonging to a Residue Class

question.text:
Which of the following integers belong to the residue class $[6]_{9}?$

  1. $-12$
  2. $3$
  3. $24$
question.explanation:
The residue class $[6]_{9}$ consists of the elements that are congruent to $6$ modulo $9.$ So, we have

\begin{align*} [6]_{9} &= \{ x \in \mathbb{Z} \: | \: x \equiv 6 \: (\text{mod}\:9) \} \\[5pt] &= \{ x \in \mathbb{Z} \: | \: x = 6 + 9k, \: k \in \mathbb{Z} \} \\[5pt] &= \{ 6 + 9k \: | \: k \in \mathbb{Z} \} \\[5pt] &= \{ \ldots, \: 6-2\cdot9, \: 6-9, \: 6, \: 6+9, \: 6+2\cdot9, \: \ldots \} \\[5pt] &= \{ \ldots, -12, -3, 6, 15, 24, \ldots \}. \end{align*}

We see that $-12$ and $24$ belong to $[6]_{9},$ while $3$ does not.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".

question.text:
Which of the following residue classes modulo $9$ contain the integer $-6?$

  1. $[2]_9$
  2. $[-3]_9$
  3. $[3]_9$
question.explanation:
We have $-6 \in [a]_{9}$ if \[ -6 \equiv a \quad (\text{mod}\:9). \]

Let's now consider each of the given equivalence classes.

  • $-6 \not\in [2]_9$ because $-6 \not\equiv 2 \: (\text{mod}\:9)$ $\quad \color{red}\times$

  • $-6 \not\in [-3]_9$ because $-6 \not\equiv -3 \: (\text{mod}\:9)$ $\quad \color{red}\times$

  • $-6 \in [3]_9$ because $-6 \equiv 3 \: (\text{mod}\:9)$ $\quad \color{green}\checkmark$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true?

  1. There are $7$ distinct residue classes modulo $8$
  2. $[4]_{6} \cap [15]_{6} \neq \emptyset$
  3. $\mathbb{Z} = [5]_{2} \cup [10]_{2}$
question.explanation:
Recall that the residue classes modulo $n$ have the following properties:

  • There are exactly $n$ distinct residue classes modulo $n$

  • Two distinct residue classes have an empty intersection: $[a]_n \cap [b]_n = \emptyset$ if $a \not\equiv b \: (\text{mod}\:n)$

  • Residue classes modulo $n$ form a partition of the set of all integers: \[\mathbb{Z} = [0]_n \cup [1]_n \cup \cdots \cup [n-1]_n\]

  • The integers modulo $n$ is defined as the set containing all distinct residue classes modulo $n$: \[\mathbb{Z}_n = \big\{[0]_n,\, [1]_n,\, \ldots,\, [n-1]_n\big\}\]

With that in mind, let's now consider each of the given statements.

  • Statement I is false. There are exactly $8$ distinct residue classes modulo $8.$

  • Statement II is false. Since $4 \not\equiv 15 \: (\text{mod }6),$ we have that $[4]_{6} \cap [15]_{6} = \emptyset.$

  • Statement III is true. First, notice the following: \begin{align*} [5]_{2} &= [1+2\cdot2]_2 = [1]_2 \\[5pt] [10]_{2} &= [0+2\cdot5]_2 = [0]_2 \\[5pt] \end{align*} As a result, we get \begin{align*} [5]_{2} \cup [10]_{2} &= [1]_{2} \cup [0]_{2} \\[5pt] &= [0]_{2} \cup [1]_{2} \\[5pt] &= \mathbb{Z} \end{align*}

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".

Which of the following statements are true?

  1. There are $3$ distinct residue classes modulo $6$
  2. $[5]_{3} \cap [1]_{3} \neq \emptyset$
  3. $\mathbb{Z} = [3]_{2} \cup [6]_{2}$
question.explanation:
Recall that the residue classes modulo $n$ have the following properties:

  • There are exactly $n$ distinct residue classes modulo $n$

  • Two distinct residue classes have an empty intersection: $[a]_n \cap [b]_n = \emptyset$ if $a \not\equiv b \: (\text{mod}\:n)$

  • Residue classes modulo $n$ form a partition of the set of all integers: \[\mathbb{Z} = [0]_n \cup [1]_n \cup \cdots \cup [n-1]_n\]

  • The integers modulo $n$ is defined as the set containing all distinct residue classes modulo $n$: \[\mathbb{Z}_n = \big\{[0]_n,\, [1]_n,\, \ldots,\, [n-1]_n\big\}\]

With that in mind, let's now consider each of the given statements.

  • Statement I is false. There are exactly $6$ distinct residue classes modulo $6.$

  • Statement II is false. Since $5 \not\equiv 1 \: (\text{mod }3),$ we have that $[5]_{3} \cap [1]_{3} = \emptyset.$

  • Statement III is true. First, notice the following: \begin{align*} [3]_{2} &= [1+2\cdot1]_2 = [1]_2 \\[5pt] [6]_{2} &= [0+2\cdot3]_2 = [0]_2 \\[5pt] \end{align*} As a result, we get \begin{align*} [3]_{2} \cup [6]_{2} &= [1]_{2} \cup [0]_{2} \\[5pt] &= [0]_{2} \cup [1]_{2} \\[5pt] &= \mathbb{Z} \end{align*}

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true?

  1. There are $9$ distinct residue classes modulo $9$
  2. $[9]_{4} \cap [5]_{4} = \emptyset$
  3. $\mathbb{Z} = [0]_{3} \cup [4]_{3} \cup [11]_{3}$
question.explanation:
Recall that the residue classes modulo $n$ have the following properties:

  • There are exactly $n$ distinct residue classes modulo $n$

  • Two distinct residue classes have an empty intersection: $[a]_n \cap [b]_n = \emptyset$ if $a \not\equiv b \: (\text{mod}\:n)$

  • Residue classes modulo $n$ form a partition of the set of all integers: \[\mathbb{Z} = [0]_n \cup [1]_n \cup \cdots \cup [n-1]_n\]

  • The integers modulo $n$ is defined as the set containing all distinct residue classes modulo $n$: \[\mathbb{Z}_n = \big\{[0]_n,\, [1]_n,\, \ldots,\, [n-1]_n\big\}\]

With that in mind, let's now consider each of the given statements.

  • Statement I is true. There are $9$ distinct residue classes modulo $9.$

  • Statement II is false. Indeed, since $9 \equiv 5 \: (\text{mod }4),$ we have that $[9]_4=[5]_4.$ Therefore, $[9]_{4} \cap [5]_{4} \neq \emptyset.$

  • Statement III is true. First, notice the following: \begin{align*} [4]_{3} &= [1+3\cdot1]_3 = [1]_3 \\[5pt] [11]_{3} &= [2+3\cdot3]_3 = [2]_3 \\[5pt] \end{align*} As a result, we get \begin{align*} [0]_{3} \cup [4]_{3} \cup [11]_{3} &= [0]_{3} \cup [1]_{3} \cup [2]_{3} \\[5pt] &= \mathbb{Z} \end{align*}

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
